We propose COCOA for controllable codeswitched generation using a machine translation‑based model where the source and target languages are monolingual Hindi text and Hindi‑English CS text, respectively.
In this paper, we tackle the problem of generating CS text from monolingual text while providing inference-time levers to control for CMI, SPI and formality of the generated CS text.

Semantic consistency with the source monolingual sentence is computed using BLEU scores between a reference CS sentence and the generated sentence. Attribute faithfulness for CMI is measured using two metrics: CMI acc and CMI corr .

guideline: Raters were asked 'How natural does the mixed language sentence sound?' with options for naturalness, and 'How well does the mixed-language sentence capture the meaning of the Hindi sentence?' with options for semantic consistency; for formality, raters were asked 'Which among the code-switched sentences is more formal?'.

Raters were shown a monolingual Hindi sentence and its generated code‑switched counterpart and asked to rate (1) how natural the mixed sentence sounds, (2) how well it captures the meaning of the Hindi sentence, and (3) which of two outputs is more formal.
